title: Visual Compliance via Executable Safety Rule Entailment
abstract: arXiv:2609.18328v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in LLMs and VLMs have enabled safety systems to reason beyond simple risk patterns toward more contextual and semantic safety concerns. However, as risk patterns continue to evolve and safety rules become more complex, existing training-based end-to-end safeguards face persistent challenges in adaptability and explainable reasoning over complex safety rules. To address these challenges, we propose GuardEn (Guarding by Safety Rule Entailment), an executable safeguard framework that decomposes safety policies into atomic propositions through Safety-Rule Compilation, modeling their composition as executable code. At test time, Scene-Grounded Execution instantiates these atomic propositions with contextual visual information derived from scene graphs, enabling rule-grounded and interpretable safety reasoning. translated_title: 通过可执行安全规则蕴含实现视觉合规
translated_abstract: 近年来大型语言模型（LLMs）和视觉语言模型（VLMs）的进展使安全系统能够超越简单的风险模式推理，转向更具上下文性和语义性的安全考量。然而，随着风险模式不断演变和安全规则日益复杂，现有的基于训练的端到端安全防护方法在适应性和对复杂安全规则的可解释推理方面持续面临挑战。为解决这些问题，我们提出了GuardEn（通过安全规则蕴含进行防护），一个可执行的安全防护框架，它通过安全规则编译将安全策略分解为原子命题，并将其组合建模为可执行代码。在测试阶段，基于场景的执行利用从场景图中获取的上下文视觉信息来实例化这些原子命题，从而实现基于规则且可解释的安全推理。在SafetyVisionBench上的实验证明了可编程安全防护在复杂视觉安全评估中的有效性。
tldr: GuardEn是一个可执行的安全防护框架，通过将安全策略编译为原子命题组成的可执行代码，并在测试时结合场景图中的视觉信息进行实例化，从而实现对复杂视觉安全问题的基于规则且可解释的推理。
en_tdlr: GuardEn is an executable safeguard framework that compiles safety policies into atomic propositions modeled as executable code and instantiates them with scene-graph-derived visual information, enabling rule-grounded and interpretable safety reasoning for complex visual safety assessment.
